sec: Fluid tapping and the grading–treatment table · p1006

items.q: The paracentesis site is the left lower quadrant, ___ cm cephalad and ___ cm medial to the ASIS:
items.exp: Fluid tapping: left lower quadrant 3 cm cephalad, 2 cm medial to ASIS; point of maximal dullness on percussion. (Book p1006)

items.q: An alternative landmark for the tapping site is:
opts: The point of maximal dullness on percussion
Mid-clavicular line at the costal margin
items.exp: Second bullet: point of maximal dullness on percussion. (Book p1006)

items.q: Grade 1 ascites is defined as mild ascites that is:
items.exp: Grade 1: mild ascites, only detectable by ultrasound; treatment — no treatment. (Book p1006)

items.q: Grade 2 ascites is defined as moderate ascites evident by:
opts: Moderate symmetrical distension of the abdomen
items.exp: Grade 2: moderate ascites evident by moderate symmetrical distension of the abdomen. (Book p1006)

items.q: Match the grade-2 diuretic ladder — 1) First diuretic 2) Its starting dose 3) Added on no response 4) Its starting dose … A) Lasix 40 mg/d B) Spironolactone 100 mg/d C) 40 mg/d D) 100 mg/d
items.exp: Diuretics: spironolactone 100 mg/d (max 400 mg/d); on no response Lasix 40 mg/d (max 160 mg/d); then refractory ascites. (Book p1006)

items.q: The maximum daily doses printed are spironolactone 400 mg/d and Lasix:
items.exp: Lasix 40 mg/d (max dose : 160 mg/d); spironolactone 100 mg/d (max dose 400 mg/d). (Book p1006)

items.q: Grade 2 ascites management includes dietary restriction of sodium intake to:
items.exp: Grade 2 treatment: restriction of sodium intake 2 g/day — degraded in print as 'a g/day'. (Book p1006)

items.q: Grade 3 ascites (large, marked distension) is initially managed by:
opts: Large-volume paracentesis, then sodium restriction + diuretics (unless refractory)
High-dose spironolactone monotherapy alone titrated up to 400 mg daily
Primary emergent TIPSS placement as the initial therapeutic procedure
Strict dietary sodium and fluid restriction without any paracentesis
items.exp: Grade 3: large volume paracentesis followed by restriction of sodium intake and diuretics (unless refractory ascites); on no response → TIPSS. (Book p1006)

items.q: In grade-3 management, TIPSS is reached after:
opts: No response to paracentesis + sodium restriction + diuretics
items.exp: Grade 3 arrow: no response → TIPSS (Transjugular Intrahepatic Porto Systemic Shunt). (Book p1006)

items.q: The closing line under ascites grading recommendations instructs:
opts: Always look for JVP for constrictions
items.exp: Bottom line: always look for JVP for constrictions — i.e., check the JVP for constrictive pericarditis in a patient with ascites. (Book p1006)
